title: Runaway adventure with little Willie Watson
summary: As a three- or four-year-old he wandered off with a spoiled neighbour boy, Willie Watson, and the two ended up at the police station, where Willie screamed and rolled on the floor until given ice cream.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: (Inaudible) slapped me three times and all of a sudden, I made it. So I kept all of these things in mind and then I remember various little small things about having my little childish ideas and dreams. I had a hobby horse (inaudible), but I put a (unintelli- gible) on it and I was driving this hobby horse (inaudible). Then I remember -- now I remember we moved from E Street to I Street and there was a little fella whose name was William Watson. I believe his father was Haitian because my mother was speaking a language to him and they were communicating and this man was a very hot-tempered man and he was a very proud man. He had a little restaurant and Willie was the only child and they spoiled Willie. Poor Willie, he -- "I want candy," and they give him candy. So Willie, one time we took a little adventure, we wanted to move out from our little section. So it seemed like we walked say from Virginia Avenue up to Dupont Circle -- that's a long way for two little fellas -- and then it seems as though
Willie got excited and started making a lot of those sounds and making a lot of crying and sounded terriable and I didn't appreciate him. I didn't appreciate that. So --

And we made so much noise until the police come and took us to the station house and it seems as though Willie wasn't satisfied with crying. He got on the floor and started rolling on the floor and then I jumped on Willie.

I said, 'Why are you making this noise?' And so he says, 'Well, ask Willie where he lives.' And Willie didn't know nothing. I says where I live, on 2219 E Street, and I know you catch the F train when you go home and that's where I live and I can get home, if I could get -- let me take him home. So then they went and got my mother and Willie went into his act until they give Willie a whole lot of ice cream. We were never friends after that. I wouldn't take Willie nowhere with me. Willie was one of those type of fellas who want to take you somewhere. So from that day on, no one takes me nowhere. No one.
